title: Prepopulating Audit Workpapers with Prior Year Assessments: Default Option Effects on Risk Rating Accuracy

scopes.description: Full author-documented experiment-data workflow: manual Excel construction of accuracy, stick-with-last-year, Work Fast and cognitive-process measures; SPSS ANOVAs, Preacher-Hayes Model 4 mediation/exploratory analyses, and Model 7 moderated mediation; AMOS SEM for Figures 2–4 and low/high multi-group moderation for each moderator. The supplied package includes experimental materials and Appendix C prior-year crosswalk but no participant responses or executable program.

requirements.description: Author-prepared participant-level data/workbook for the n=117 experiment, containing current-year risk ratings and evidence text for 19 factors, prepopulation assignment, task timing and the three measured moderator responses, with enough raw information to reproduce the documented Excel measures unless they are already author-prepared. Prior-year ratings/evidence are supplied separately in Appendix C. Exact file/format, field names, prepared-measure state, guidance-condition coding, and compatible delivery route are not established.

issues.description: The three archive members are PDFs. The item 5 file gives substantial manual Excel/SPSS/AMOS procedures and illustrative function names, but supplies no executable analysis/preparation program, workbook, SPSS syntax file, or AMOS project; there is no executable entry point.

The required n=117 participant-response dataset is absent. The datasheet reports author access/retention but does not identify an input file, schema, prepared-measure state, or delivery route; access availability is unknown, not a confirmed barrier.

The instrument names General Guidance and Task-Specific Guidance screens, while the item 5 analysis recipe describes prepopulation and three measured moderators. The archive does not map those guidance conditions to participant coding/sample or analyses, nor include the model diagrams/variable-path details for referenced Figures 2–4; their role must be clarified without adding tests or assuming exclusions.

The documented spreadsheet/SPSS/AMOS and Preacher-Hayes macro targets are not verified locally. The bounded command checks establish LibreOffice availability only; they do not establish absence of other GUI/licensed applications or confirm compatibility of the workbook/macro.

evidence.description: The authors report that they conducted data collection and analysis and had access to the data.
evidence.quote:
Item 1. Tracie Majors and Stacey Ritter handled the data collection and conducted the data

evidence.description: The authors identify SPSS with the Preacher-Hayes macro and AMOS for SEM.

Item 4. See supplemental file for a copy of the experimental materials. For data analysis, we

(for Structural Equations Modeling), following the steps described in the paper and additional

using behavioral measures. Finally, we examined three (measured) auditor characteristics

evidence.description: Accuracy totals are constructed in the Excel data file for increased, decreased and unchanged risks.
evidence.quote:
Risk Assessment Accuracy: We calculated risk assessment accuracy within the Excel data file,
separately for increasing, decreasing, and no change risks.
 For the eight increasing risks, we created an indicator variable for each risk factor that
   equaled “1” if the participant correctly increased the risk from the prior year rating, and “0”
   otherwise. The sum of these eight cells equals Accuracy for Increasing Risk Factors.

evidence.description: The stick-with-last-year mediator is constructed in Excel by summing prior-year choices from the other risk groups.
evidence.quote:
Then, we calculated the mediators in Excel as follows:
 Stick with Last Year for increasing risks was the sum of the above measure for decreasing
   and no change risks.
 Stick with Last Year for decreasing risks was the sum of the above measure for increasing
   and no change risks.
 Stick with Last Year for no change risks was the sum of the above measure for increasing and
   decreasing risks.

evidence.description: Work Fast uses Qualtrics task timing and the documented 69 words-per-minute adjustment.
evidence.quote:
o We asked ten staff auditors to type a passage from our case study, and calculated an
          average typing time of 69 words per minute.
      o We then estimated the time participants in the prepopulated workpaper condition
          spent typing by dividing the number of new words of evidence they provided (i.e.,
          incremental to the prior year’s evidence that was prepopulated in the workpaper) by
          69, and subtracted this estimate from their total time spent on the risk assessment
          task. To count new words of evidence, we utilized the “LEN(TRIM),”
          “LEN(SUBSTITUTE),” and “ISNUMBER(SEARCH)” Excel tools.

evidence.quote:
Motivated Reasoning: We measured motivated reasoning by counting the number of transition
words indicative of counterargument within the Excel file containing participants’ documented
evidence. We performed the count separately for increasing and decreasing risk factors. To
perform the count, we utilized the “ISNUMBER(SEARCH)” Excel tool. The list of

evidence.description: Superficial processing is measured as counts of new evidence words.
evidence.quote:
Superficial Processing: We measured superficial processing by counting the number of new
words within the Excel file containing participants’ documented evidence. We performed the
count separately for increasing and decreasing risk factors. To perform the count, we utilized the
“LEN(TRIM),” “LEN(SUBSTITUTE),” and “ISNUMBER(SEARCH)” Excel tools.

evidence.description: H1/H2 use SPSS ANOVAs for accuracy of increased, decreased and unchanged risk assessments.
evidence.quote:
We first ran ANOVAs (using the SPSS menu commands: Analyze  General Linear Model 
Univariate) for the effect of our manipulated independent variable (Prepopulation) on each of
our dependent variables (Accuracy for Increasing, Decreasing, and No Change Risks). This
analysis provides our tests of H1 and H2 (the effects of prepopulation of workpapers on risk
rating accuracy, for changing and unchanged risks, respectively). The ANOVA results are
tabulated in Table 1, Panel C.

evidence.description: H3/H4 use AMOS SEM and the Preacher-Hayes Model 4 macro; Model 4 also supports exploratory cognitive-process analyses.
evidence.quote:
We used two statistical methods for tests of H3 and H4 (our hypotheses about auditors’
responses to prepopulated workpapers, and how these responses mediate the relation between
prepopulation and risk rating accuracy). Specifically, we used structural equation modeling
(using AMOS software) and the Preacher and Hayes [2008] bias-corrected bootstrapping method
using the Preacher and Hayes macro in SPSS.

evidence.description: AMOS models use Figures 2–4 with residual error terms.
evidence.quote:
Figures 2-4 display our empirical models that we tested using both approaches.
 Structural Equations Modeling: We used the AMOS graphics tool to draw the empirical
   models displayed in Figures 2-4, also including residual error terms on the mediators and
   dependent variable. We then ran each model by clicking the “Calculate Estimates” icon in
   AMOS. The AMOS output provided the estimates and goodness of fit statistics.

evidence.description: AMOS compares unconstrained and constrained models using low/high moderator groups, for increasing and decreasing risks.
evidence.quote:
The first approach was a comparison of two structural equations models within AMOS – one that
was unconstrained (i.e., the models displayed in Figures 2-4), and one that constrained the links
between the independent variable (Prepopulation) and the mediators (Stick with Last Year and
Work Fast) to be equal across levels of the moderator being examined. This approach is
illustrated in detail in Arbuckle [2016].
 Using “Manage Groups,” we created three groups within AMOS for each moderator (low,
    medium, and high). These groups were based on the closest cutoffs to achieve an even split
    across the three levels. To conduct the strongest test of moderation, for this analysis, we
    compared two groups: the low and high groups.

evidence.description: The Preacher-Hayes Model 7 analysis adds continuous moderators to Figures 2–3 for changing risks.
evidence.quote:
The second approach was the Preacher and Hayes [2007] moderated-mediation method using the
Preacher and Hayes macro. We used the same process/macro as described for the test of
mediation (i.e., tests of H1 and H2), but instead used “Model 7,” which incorporates the
continuous moderators in the empirical models (i.e., adds the moderators to the empirical models
displayed in Figures 2-3, i.e., just for changing risks). The Preacher and Hayes macro output
provided the confidence intervals testing for moderation of the mediators.

evidence.quote:

evidence.description: All conditions have access to the prior-year ratings and evidence in Appendix C.
evidence.quote:
These workpapers are for auditors in the Prepopulation condition. Auditors in the Non-
Prepopulation condition view the same workpapers, but the workpapers are blank (i.e., do not
contain the prior year risk ratings and evidence). Note that auditors in all experimental
conditions have access to these prior year risk ratings and evidence (in the Prior Year Risk
Assessment file, displayed in Appendix C).

actions.description: No executable program is supplied, but the datasheet documents a manual GUI workflow. Once the input, design mapping and software are confirmed, follow that procedure and retain all reported analysis branches.
steps: In the author workbook, compute the three accuracy totals from the 8 increasing, 6 decreasing, and 5 unchanged factors; construct Stick with Last Year by the documented cross-group sums.

Compute Work Fast from Qualtrics task time using the stated 69 words-per-minute scalar: estimate prepopulated-condition typing time from new evidence words/69 and subtract it from raw time; also compute average non-prepopulated typing time from average words/69 and add that estimate to each prepopulated participant’s time, as described.

Calculate motivated-reasoning transition-word counts and new-word counts separately for increasing and decreasing risks, using the documented word list and Excel functions; use the documented professional-identity, reverse-scored Replenishment, and prepopulated-workpaper-use moderator measures.

Run SPSS GLM univariate ANOVAs for the three accuracy outcomes (H1/H2), then the documented Preacher-Hayes Model 4 mediation models for Figures 2–4 and exploratory cognitive-process analyses, retaining the stated 90% bias-corrected bootstrap intervals.
Run the AMOS structural equation models for Figures 2–4 with residual error terms on mediators and dependent variables; record estimates and fit statistics.

For each of the three moderators, create the documented low/medium/high groups using closest even-split cutoffs and perform the low/high AMOS multi-group comparison by constraining Prepopulation-to-mediator paths, separately for increasing and decreasing risks.
Run the Preacher-Hayes Model 7 moderated-mediation models with continuous moderators for Figures 2–3/changing risks.
validation: Compare the H1/H2 ANOVA results to Table 1, Panel C and compare all mediation/moderation outputs with the paper’s specified tables/figures after obtaining the missing model definitions.
Record software versions, input field mappings, exclusions and manual GUI settings; leave execution_verified false until an authorized execution is completed.

review_notes: The item 5 datasheet is a substantive manual/GUI recipe, not an executable program: isolated Excel function names do not constitute a supplied formula workbook or driver.

The experiment sample is n=117. No analysis-ready participant-response data are in the three-PDF archive. Do not recreate or recollect responses; request the author-prepared input and its format/route.

Appendix C pages 28–30 contain the prior-year ratings/evidence for all 19 risk factors; this packaged crosswalk is credited. The 69 words-per-minute scalar is given in the datasheet, so the historical ten-person typing exercise is not a separate live data requirement.

All documented analysis branches are retained: three accuracy ANOVAs, Figure 2–4 SEM and Model 4 analyses including exploratory cognitive processes, AMOS low/high moderation for three moderator constructs by increasing/decreasing risks, and Model 7 continuous moderated mediation for changing risks in Figures 2–3.

General Guidance and Task-Specific Guidance screens are present in the instrument; their relationship to the reported prepopulation analyses remains an explicit clarification, not an assumed extra test or exclusion. Visual inspection confirmed that the item 5 pages do not include the referenced Figure 2–4 model diagrams.

No analysis-only scope is justified without a supported compatible participant-data route. No author programs were executed and no participant-level analysis dataset was read; visual inspection was limited to the supplied instrument/reference and method pages.
